picks.t: Golden State Valkyries WNBA Playoff Game 4
picks.d: The Valkyries are in the WNBA Semifinals and Game 4 against the defending champion Las Vegas Aces is at Chase Center — IF necessary. They're up 1-0 in the series after a dominant 71-60 win, so this could be a series-clinching home game. Do NOT sleep on this — it's the most electric sports moment SF has had in years.

picks.t: My Morning Jacket — Fillmore Residency (Final Weekend)
picks.d: The last three nights of MMJ's legendary 7-show Fillmore residency — and each night gets its own unique setlist. If you've been on the fence all week, this is your last chance. Two-plus hours of sprawling, psychedelic rock in one of the best rooms in America? Yes please.

picks.t: AURA at Grace Cathedral — Immersive Light & Sound
picks.d: Moment Factory transforms Grace Cathedral into a breathtaking, seven-chapter journey of projection mapping and original music. Friday night has a special live music prelude before the main experience. It's honestly one of those SF nights that feels kind of unreal — a Gothic cathedral turned into a living work of art.

picks.t: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
picks.d: BTS's RM has spent nearly a decade quietly building a serious art collection, and now almost 150 works from that collection are sharing walls with SFMOMA's own — making this one of the largest presentations of Korean modern art in the US. Whether you're a BTS fan or a full-on art nerd, this is genuinely a big deal.

Fleet Week is still going and Chinatown is turning up with its annual Night Market — food vendors, cultural performances, open-air shopping, and that unmistakable Friday-night-in-SF energy. It's completely free and one of the most fun ways to kick off the weekend.

picks.t: Parade of Ships Under the Golden Gate Bridge
picks.d: Fleet Week's iconic Parade of Ships rolls under the Golden Gate as part of the last big day of the celebration. Head to Crissy Field for one of the most jaw-dropping, only-in-SF free spectacles of the entire year. Bring a jacket, grab a coffee, and just soak it in.

picks.t: Kat Robichaud's Misfit Cabaret: Final Girl
picks.d: This is the one. SF's ultimate Halloween theatrical experience is back at GAMH — rock, burlesque, comedy, and jaw-dropping costumes collide in one spectacular Saturday night. It's part of Psyched! Fest 2026 and tickets run $50–$500, so go ahead and treat yourself.

picks.t: Sex Pistols (Jones, Cook & Matlock) at The Warfield
picks.d: Three founding members of the most iconic punk band in history. One classic SF venue. One night only. Steve Jones, Paul Cook, and Glen Matlock bring the raw, anarchic energy of the Sex Pistols to the Warfield — this is the kind of show you tell people about for the next twenty years.

picks.t: Lucania — New Opening at the Ferry Building
picks.d: The team behind A16 is taking over one of the Ferry Building's most prominent spaces with Lucania, a southern Italian spot focused on little fish — marinated anchovies, roasted sardines, steamed mussels — plus killer pastas and pizzas. It's the most exciting new table in SF right now.

picks.t: SF Indigenous Peoples Day — Yerba Buena Gardens
picks.d: The International Indian Treaty Council and the Yerba Buena Gardens Festival present a free outdoor celebration featuring a special performance by acclaimed artist Jeremy Dutcher. A meaningful, beautiful way to spend your Monday afternoon in the heart of the city.

picks.t: Young Miko — Late Checkout Tour at Chase Center
picks.d: Puerto Rican reggaeton and trap star Young Miko is one of Latin music's fastest-rising acts, and her Chase Center debut is the hottest Latin show of the fall. Sharp lyrics, infectious beats, arena energy — and tickets start at just $59, which is a genuinely great deal for this level of show.

To celebrate the RM exhibition, SFMOMA is throwing a K-pop party on the rooftop. Music, dancing, community, and views — the perfect Thursday night if you've been to the show already (or haven't yet and want the full experience). This is going to be a vibe.

picks.t: Divine Offering: Celebrating Alice Coltrane at GAMH
picks.d: Alice Coltrane's own family leads this deeply spiritual tribute to one of the most visionary jazz composers and harpists of the 20th century. Featuring Sita Michelle Coltrane and special guests, this is the kind of show that genuinely transcends a normal night out. Part of Psyched! Fest 2026.

picks.t: Haunted Halloween Hoopla Artisan Night Market
picks.d: The spooky season is officially on at Fifty Vara's free outdoor night market — food, drinks, retail, artisan vendors, and full Halloween energy. It's family-friendly, totally free, and a great way to close out the week before heading somewhere for the night.

ongoing.d: Immersive Moment Factory projection experience running nightly through October — seven chapters of light, music, and magic inside a Gothic cathedral.

ongoing.t: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
ongoing.d: Nearly 150 works from RM's personal art collection alongside SFMOMA's own, running through February 7, 2027.

ongoing.t: Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc at SFMOMA
ongoing.d: 75,000 hand-crafted kites transformed into a floating cloudscape in the Roberts Family Gallery — free to see on Floor 1.

ongoing.t: de Young: Treasures of the Pharaohs
ongoing.d: Running through January 31 at the de Young in Golden Gate Park — free Saturdays for Bay Area residents.

ongoing.t: Asian Art Museum: Ha Chong-Hyun Retrospective
ongoing.d: A major retrospective of the Korean artist's tactile, immersive work, running through January 25, 2027.
Blue Angels, ship tours, and waterfront events through October 12 — all free along the northern waterfront.
Giant digital artworks projected onto the historic Humboldt Bank Building at 785 Market St., nightly through October.

new.name: Lucania
new.d: From the A16 team: southern Italian pastas, pizzas, and a 'Pesce Blu' section starring sardines, anchovies, and mussels in SF's best dining room.

new.name: Olive Juice
new.d: Divisadero's newest morning spot doing olive oil smoothies, salads, and an Olive Oil Cacao Espresso that sounds wild and tastes great — open Thu–Sun.

new.name: Shinka
new.d: A sleek new tasting menu experience inside The Jay Hotel in FiDi — the most ambitious new opening in SF this month.

new.name: Bayview Oyster Bar
new.d: Grilled and raw oysters, clam chowder, and Dungeness crab with garlic noodles from the chef behind the beloved Auntie April's — a neighborhood gem worth the trip.

new.name: 15 Romolo
new.d: The 115-year-old pseudo-speakeasy tucked down a North Beach alley just finished a two-year renovation — back and better, with Pimm's cups and sherry in a refreshed interior.

classic.name: Maria Isabel
classic.d: From the Dalida team: a seasonally changing menu with local shrimp aguachile and tamales de elote that are dialed all the way up.

classic.name: Ah Ma's Kitchen
classic.d: Hong Kong flavors and Cantonese comfort food on Clement Street — one of Yelp's Best New Restaurants of 2026 and a neighborhood gem.

classic.name: Bar Coto
classic.d: The Cotogna team's walk-in-only spot for coffee, sandwiches, and excellent gelato by day, small plates and great cocktails by night.

classic.name: A16
classic.d: The original Neapolitan pizza and southern Italian institution that spawned Lucania — still one of the best wood-fired pies in the city.

classic.name: Cotogna
classic.d: Rustic Italian-inspired cooking at its finest — if Bar Coto has a wait next door, you're at the right place either way.

bars.name: Rye Cocktail Bar
bars.d: Sleek downtown cocktail bar hosting a singles speed dating event Thursday — but worth visiting any night for its serious drink program.

bars.name: 15 Romolo
bars.d: Just reopened after a two-year renovation — the bohemian North Beach speakeasy alley bar is back with Pimm's cups, sherry, and good vibes.

bars.name: Bar Coto
bars.d: Coffee and gelato by day, small plates and sharp cocktails by night — a perfect pre-dinner or late-night stop in Jackson Square.

bars.name: Alameda Brewing
bars.d: Hosting back-to-back speed dating events Friday night, but genuinely a great East Bay spot for craft beer any time of the week.

bars.name: Halcyon SF
bars.d: Restored early-1900s brick-and-steel warehouse on 11th St with state-of-the-art sound and a fiercely loyal electronic music crowd.

bars.name: Public Works
bars.d: One of SF's most beloved underground clubs — intimate, eclectic, and hosting Roam's 25th anniversary with Man Power on Friday night.

bars.name: 1015 Folsom
bars.d: SF's underground institution since 1986 — big rooms, serious sound, and a legacy that makes it the anchor of the SoMa club scene every weekend.

bars.name: Rick & Roxy's
bars.d: Casual, fun Marina District bar hosting a Cityswoon speed dating night Tuesday — and a solid neighborhood hangout the rest of the week.

games.detail: WNBA Semifinals Game 4 — Valkyries lead series 1-0. This could be a series-clinching home game. Do not miss this.
WNBA Semifinals Game 5 — only if necessary. Chase Center.

sports.note: The Valkyries finished 32-12 and lead the league in defensive rating. This is SF's hottest sports ticket right now.

games.detail: NBA Preseason — the Warriors are rebuilding after Jimmy Butler's ACL injury last January. A low-stakes, fun way to kick off the new season.

sports.note: Away game Tuesday vs. Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas if you're feeling adventurous.

concerts.d: The final three nights of MMJ's epic 7-show Fillmore residency. Each night is a different setlist — the Louisville rockers are known for sprawling, psychedelic sets that run well past two hours. If you only catch one of the three, Sunday is typically the most emotional closer.

concerts.t: Sex Pistols (Steve Jones, Paul Cook & Glen Matlock)
concerts.d: Three founding members of punk's most iconic band, one night only at The Warfield. Raw, anarchic, and utterly unrepeatable — this is the kind of show that belongs on a bucket list. Expect wall-to-wall classics and zero apologies.

Puerto Rican reggaeton and trap star Young Miko is one of Latin music's fastest-rising names, and her Chase Center stop is the hottest Latin show of the fall. Sharp lyricism, infectious beats, and arena-scale energy — and tickets start at just $59.

concerts.t: Rod Wave — Don't Look Down Tour
concerts.d: One of rap's most emotionally resonant voices hits Chase Center for a night of melodic rap and raw storytelling. Rod Wave's fanbase is devoted for a reason — the energy in that room is going to be something else.

concerts.w: Fri Oct 9 & Sat Oct 10 · 7:30pm / Sun Oct 11 · 2pm
concerts.d: Rachmaninoff's final orchestral composition is one of the most dramatic and nostalgically beautiful works in the entire classical canon. The SF Symphony does it justice every single time — three chances to catch it this weekend.

The Italian composer behind billions of streams plays Davies Symphony Hall alone — just him and a grand piano in one of SF's most magnificent rooms. His minimalist, deeply moving compositions hit differently in person. This is genuinely rare.

The Puerto Rican Latin pop icon has been electrifying audiences for decades with charismatic dancing and romantic ballads. 'Let's Dance Again' is exactly the right energy for a Sunday night, and Chase Center is going to be electric.

concerts.t: Kelsey Lu — So Help Me God Tour
concerts.d: A classically trained cellist and avant-garde R&B artist whose live shows are emotionally overwhelming, visually stunning, and utterly unlike anything else you'll see this year. GAMH is the perfect intimate room for her.

Camilo Lara's acclaimed electronic project blends cumbia, electronic beats, and Latin pop into a wildly danceable and culturally rich experience. With support from Spaghetti Cumbia, Edgar, and Kaefan — this midweek party is going OFF.

Three of the world's most celebrated classical soloists on one stage — Lisa Batiashvili on violin, Renaud Capuçon on violin, and Jean-Yves Thibaudet on piano. This is an extraordinary musical event, full stop. Chamber music doesn't get more refined than this.

concertsOngoing.d: Davies Symphony Hall hosts concerts nearly every night this week — check sfsymphony.org for the full schedule and last-minute ticket deals.

concertsOngoing.t: Great American Music Hall: Psyched! Fest 2026
concertsOngoing.d: GAMH's multi-night festival runs all week with Provoker (Tue), Mexican Institute of Sound (Wed), and Kelsey Lu (Thu) still to come.

singles.t: SF Speed Dating @ Alameda Brewing — Ages 44–59 & 29–49
singles.d: Pre-Dating has facilitated over 5 million mini-dates since 2001, and this Friday they're running two back-to-back events at Alameda Brewing. The 44–59 crowd goes first at 6:30pm, followed by the 29–49 group at 8:15pm — so you could technically do both if you're ambitious.

singles.t: The Speed Dating Alternative SF at O'Reilly's Pub
singles.d: Billed as 'an immersive singles group date for people who want more than small talk across a table' — think games, challenges, and organic mingling at a classic SF pub. Way less stiff than traditional speed dating, and honestly more fun for it.

singles.t: Cityswoon Midweek Date Night — Marina District, Ages 30–45
singles.d: Cityswoon's 'Speed Dating 2.0' uses a smart-matching algorithm to pair you throughout the night at Rick & Roxy's in the Marina — so instead of a boring round-robin, you're only meeting people you're actually compatible with. Tuesday night, Marina vibes, good people.

singles.t: Black & Dating: Black-Centered Singles Mixer, Open to All
singles.d: An inclusive, community-focused singles mixer at DACHA Kitchen & Bar in Lower Nob Hill — good food, good drinks, and real conversations in a relaxed setting. Exactly the kind of low-pressure social event that's actually fun to attend.

singles.t: Volo Sports: Glow Kickball + Flip Cup League Kickoff
singles.d: Volo's coed Glow Kickball + Flip Cup league launches at Mission Dolores Park this Thursday — and honestly, joining a sports league is one of the best ways to meet people in SF. Volo runs leagues in kickball, volleyball, pickleball, and more all over the city.

singles.t: Roam x Sirens: Man Power — 25 Years of Roam at Public Works
singles.d: Roam Recordings' 25th anniversary party at Public Works is an RA Pick and one of the best underground club nights of the week. Man Power brings a wide range of feel-good tunes, the crowd is always friendly and unpretentious, and Public Works is one of the best small clubs in America.

singlesOngoing.t: Run Club SF — Tues, Thurs & Sat
singlesOngoing.d: Tuesday nights in Golden Gate Park, Thursday speedwork at Kezar Stadium, Saturday adventure runs — one of the best free ways to meet active people in SF.
2,386 members, 5-star rating, Sunday 10am at the Panhandle — all paces welcome, optional coffee after. Zero intimidation, maximum good vibes.

date.title: Fleet Week Finale + Farmers Market Morning
date.tagline: The most impressive free first date SF can offer

steps.title: Parade of Ships Under the Golden Gate
steps.detail: Head to Crissy Field for the Fleet Week Parade of Ships — watching military vessels pass under the Golden Gate Bridge is one of those moments that makes people fall in love with this city (and possibly each other).

steps.title: Walk the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Stroll through the Ferry Building — grab a coffee, share a snack from one of the vendors, and peek into Lucania if it's open yet. The vibe is relaxed, there's always something interesting to look at, and the Embarcadero views are unbeatable.

steps.title: Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc at SFMOMA
steps.detail: The Floor 1 installation at SFMOMA is completely free to see — 75,000 hand-crafted kites turned into a floating cloudscape. It's genuinely stunning and takes about 20 minutes. Great conversation starter.

steps.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated (Evening Preview Walk)
steps.detail: Wander down to 785 Market St before sunset to position yourselves for the nightly digital art projection on the Humboldt Bank Building. Grab a bench in Yerba Buena Gardens while you wait — the gardens are free and beautiful.

date.title: North Beach Reopening + Psyched! Fest
date.tagline: Cocktails in a 115-year-old alley bar, then live music at GAMH

steps.title: Drinks at 15 Romolo
steps.detail: The freshly renovated North Beach pseudo-speakeasy just reopened after two years. Order a Pimm's cup or a sherry, find a corner in the refreshed interior, and enjoy the fact that you're in a bar that's been here since 1911.

steps.title: Dinner at a North Beach Classic
steps.detail: Walk to dinner nearby — North Beach has no shortage of Italian spots. Keep it simple: pasta, wine, good bread. You're building up to a big night.

steps.title: Kelsey Lu at Great American Music Hall (Thu) or Kat Robichaud's Misfit Cabaret (Sat)
steps.detail: Kelsey Lu's avant-garde R&B cello performance on Thursday is emotionally stunning and unlike anything else. Saturday's Misfit Cabaret is the ultimate SF theatrical Halloween extravaganza. Pick your night, pick your vibe.

date.title: AURA at Grace Cathedral + Dinner in Nob Hill
date.tagline: The most romantic night in SF this week, no contest

steps.title: Dinner in Nob Hill
steps.detail: Start with an elegant dinner in Nob Hill — you're near Grace Cathedral, so take your time and let dinner stretch into real conversation.

steps.title: AURA at Grace Cathedral — Live Music Prelude (Fri Oct 9)
steps.detail: Friday night has a special live music performance before the main AURA experience — arrive early enough to catch it. Then settle in for the full seven-chapter immersive projection journey inside the Cathedral.

steps.title: Nightcap at a Nob Hill Bar
steps.detail: After AURA you'll want to sit quietly with a drink and talk about what you just experienced. Nob Hill has several good hotel bars for exactly this — unhurried, elegant, and a perfect end to the evening.

solo.title: SF Indigenous Peoples Day + Free Art Tour
solo.tagline: Culture, community, and world-class art without spending a dime

steps.title: SF Indigenous Peoples Day at Yerba Buena Gardens
steps.detail: Jeremy Dutcher performs at this free outdoor celebration at Yerba Buena Gardens. It's meaningful, beautiful, and the kind of event that reminds you why living in SF is special.

steps.title: Walk to SFMOMA — Free Floor 1
steps.detail: Pop into SFMOMA to see the Jacob Hashimoto Giant Arc installation on Floor 1 — it's free, it's stunning, and it's one block away. If you want to go upstairs, the RM exhibition is $10 weekdays.

steps.title: Minnesota Street Project in Dogpatch
steps.detail: Hop on the T-Third to Dogpatch and spend an afternoon at Minnesota Street Project — free galleries open Wed–Sat 12–5pm with shows including Character Development and Alex Weinstein through Oct 17.

solo.title: Museum Deep Dive + Lunchtime Concert
solo.tagline: A full, satisfying day of art and music on your own schedule

steps.title: de Young Museum — Treasures of the Pharaohs
steps.detail: Spend a leisurely morning at the de Young in Golden Gate Park. The Pharaohs exhibition is running through January and the park walk in is half the fun. Saturday is free for Bay Area residents.

steps.title: Free Lunchtime Concert at Yerba Buena Gardens (Thu Oct 15)
steps.detail: Richard Howell performs a free outdoor concert at the Great Lawn from 12:30–1:30pm on Thursday. Pack a lunch or grab something nearby and eat outside.

steps.title: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
steps.detail: Spend the afternoon with the RM exhibition — $10 on weekdays, $12 weekends. Budget for a couple of hours: there's a lot to see and it rewards slow looking.

steps.title: Exploratorium After Dark: Speak Easy (Thu Oct 15)
steps.detail: End the week at Exploratorium After Dark — decode hidden patterns in communication, try brand-new activities, and enjoy the adults-only vibe at Pier 15. ~$20 entry.

solo.title: World-Class Classical Music Marathon
solo.tagline: Three extraordinary concerts in one week — pick your night

steps.title: SF Symphony: Rachmaninoff Symphonic Dances at Davies
steps.detail: Rachmaninoff's final orchestral work, performed by the SF Symphony. Brooding, nostalgic, dramatic — this is serious concert-going. Three performances this weekend.

steps.title: Ludovico Einaudi Solo Piano at Davies
steps.detail: The Italian composer plays Davies Symphony Hall alone. Solo piano in a grand hall is one of the most intimate concert experiences you can have — and Einaudi's minimalism lands differently live than on a playlist.

steps.title: Batiashvili / Capuçon / Thibaudet Trio at Davies
steps.detail: Three of the world's best classical soloists on one stage. This chamber trio is genuinely rare — book it now and treat yourself to dinner at Bar Coto beforehand.

birthday.title: Birthday Parade of Ships
birthday.tagline: A birthday morning that's legitimately iconic

steps.title: Coffee at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Start the birthday morning right — grab a great coffee from one of the Ferry Building's rotating vendors and enjoy it on the waterfront. The light is beautiful and it's all free.

steps.title: Parade of Ships at Crissy Field (Fri Oct 9)
steps.detail: Walk or Lyft to Crissy Field for the Fleet Week Parade of Ships under the Golden Gate. This is a legitimately great birthday moment — military vessels, the Bridge, the Bay.

steps.title: Chinatown Night Market (Fri Oct 9 · 5–9pm)
steps.detail: Come back in the evening for the Chinatown Night Market — birthday dinner from food vendors, cultural performances, and open-air festivity. Free, festive, and fun.

birthday.title: Misfit Cabaret Birthday Spectacular
birthday.tagline: Kat Robichaud's Halloween cabaret was basically made for birthdays

steps.title: Pre-Show Drinks at 15 Romolo
steps.detail: The just-reopened North Beach speakeasy is a perfect birthday pre-game — order a round of Pimm's cups and revel in the fact that you're in a 115-year-old bar that just got a glow-up.

steps.title: Dinner in North Beach
steps.detail: Birthday dinner with the crew — North Beach Italian is always the right call. Keep it festive and don't rush.

steps.title: Kat Robichaud's Misfit Cabaret: Final Girl at GAMH
steps.detail: Rock, burlesque, comedy, and Halloween costumes in one wild Saturday night. Tickets run $50–$500 — splurge on good seats for the birthday person. This is a proper event.

birthday.title: AURA + Shinka Tasting Menu Birthday
birthday.tagline: The most special birthday night in SF this week

steps.title: Shinka Tasting Menu at The Jay Hotel
steps.detail: The new Japanese-French tasting menu inside The Jay in FiDi is the most ambitious new restaurant opening in SF this month. Birthday dinner here is a statement.

steps.title: Walk to Yerba Buena Illuminated
steps.detail: After dinner, walk to 785 Market St for the free digital art projection on the Humboldt Bank Building. A luxurious post-dinner stroll with a free visual payoff.

steps.title: AURA at Grace Cathedral (Fri Oct 9 Live Music Night)
steps.detail: End the birthday with the most stunning visual experience in SF — seven chapters of light, music, and projection mapping inside Grace Cathedral. Friday's live music prelude makes it extra special.

friends.title: Yacht Rock Block Party + Night Market
friends.tagline: Free outdoor music plus free Halloween vibes — a full free Friday

steps.title: Fridays on Front Street: Yacht Rock Block Party
steps.detail: Downtown SF Partnership and Noise Pop throw a free outdoor block party on Front Street. Live music, drinks, and smooth '70s–'80s sounds — start the Friday here.

steps.title: Grab Dinner en Route to Chinatown
steps.detail: Walk or Lyft to Chinatown and grab dinner from the vendors opening up for the Night Market — it's casual, cheap, and everyone gets to pick their own thing.

steps.title: Chinatown Night Market 2026 (Fri Oct 9 · 5–9pm)
steps.detail: Wander the Night Market together — food, cultural performances, shopping, and the festive energy of Fleet Week weekend. Completely free and one of the best group hangouts of the week.

friends.title: Valkyries Playoff Game Watch + SoMa Club Night
friends.tagline: Cheer the Valkyries on, then take the night to SoMa

steps.title: Golden State Valkyries Playoff Game 4 at Chase Center (Sun Oct 11)
steps.detail: Get tickets at valkyries.wnba.com and get to Chase Center. The Valkyries are in the WNBA Semifinals and this could be a series-clinching home game. The energy is going to be electric.

steps.title: Celebrate (Win or Lose) in SoMa
steps.detail: Head down to SoMa for drinks and dancing. 1015 Folsom, Halcyon, and Audio SF are all nearby and all have great options this week.

friends.title: My Morning Jacket Final Night + Late Dinner
friends.tagline: The perfect send-off to SF's best residency of the year

steps.title: Pre-Show Dinner at a Fillmore-Area Spot
steps.detail: The Fillmore is in the Western Addition — gather the crew for dinner nearby before the show. Keep it relaxed; you've got a long night ahead.

steps.title: My Morning Jacket at The Fillmore — Night 7 (Sun Oct 11)
steps.detail: The final night of the 7-show residency. MMJ is famous for closing out residencies with their most emotional, sprawling setlists. This is a two-plus hour experience with a unique set — you will not hear the same show twice.

steps.title: Late-Night Drinks on Divisadero
steps.detail: After the show, walk to Divisadero for late-night drinks and a debrief. This is the kind of night you'll be talking about for a while — give it the proper ending it deserves.

parents.title: Fleet Week + Golden Gate Park with the Family
parents.tagline: The kids will talk about this for years

steps.title: Parade of Ships at Crissy Field (Fri Oct 9)
steps.detail: Bring the whole family to Crissy Field for the Fleet Week Parade of Ships under the Golden Gate. It's free, it's spectacular, and kids absolutely love it. Arrive early for a good spot.

steps.title: Picnic in the Presidio
steps.detail: Pack a picnic or grab food from a nearby café and eat in the Presidio — you're already there and the grounds are gorgeous in October.

steps.title: de Young Museum — Free Saturday for Bay Area Residents
steps.detail: On Saturday, Bay Area residents with valid ID get in free. The Treasures of the Pharaohs exhibition is genuinely great for kids — ancient Egypt, big artifacts, real wow moments.

parents.title: SFMOMA Family Day + Ferry Building Lunch
parents.tagline: Art, food, and a waterfront afternoon the whole family will love

steps.title: Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc at SFMOMA (Floor 1 — Free)
steps.detail: Start with the free Floor 1 installation — 75,000 kites floating in a cloudscape. Kids are completely mesmerized by it. Spend as long as you want; there's no ticket needed.

steps.title: RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
steps.detail: $10/adult weekdays — younger kids are free. The RM exhibition is visually rich and engaging enough to hold attention. Give yourselves 90 minutes to go through it properly.

steps.title: Lunch at the Ferry Building
steps.detail: Walk down to the Ferry Building for lunch — everyone picks their own thing from different vendors, you eat on the waterfront, and the kids can watch the ferries. Classic SF afternoon.

parents.title: AURA at Grace Cathedral — The Family Magic Night
parents.tagline: An immersive cathedral experience kids and parents will never forget

steps.title: Dinner in Nob Hill
steps.detail: Start with an early dinner in Nob Hill — the neighborhood has good options at multiple price points, and eating early means the kids aren't hungry during the show.

steps.title: Walk to Grace Cathedral
steps.detail: It's a short walk from most Nob Hill restaurants to Grace Cathedral at 1100 California St. The Cathedral itself is worth seeing from the outside before you go in.

steps.title: AURA at Grace Cathedral
steps.detail: Seven chapters of immersive light, music, and projection mapping inside the Cathedral. AURA is designed for all ages — the visuals are stunning, the music is original, and watching kids experience it is honestly its own kind of magic. From $24.27/person.
